Subject: Acme POC: Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the POC: 

Summary of discovery:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer-support summarization pipeline with streaming latency <= 200ms per token and average inference cost target <$0.0009/token.
- Scope: 2-week trial against a subset (~10k weekly requests) of live support transcripts; evaluate generation quality, latency, and cost.
- Integrations: Use Redwood SDK in your backend service, streaming responses to your web socket layer, and verify tool-calling for asynchronous knowledge-base lookups.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile request-to-first-token < 250ms in your staging region (US-WEST).
2) Quality: Rouge-L / human score on 200-sample evaluation set >= baseline by +5% or parity with human summaries.
3) Cost: Estimated per-token cost <= $0.001 in production profile with recommended batching/caching.
4) Reliability: No more than 1% error rate on inference calls during trial.

Owners & timelines:
- Acme engineering owner: Jordan Meyers 
— integration + test harness (target: Nov 30 for initial integration).
- Redwood SE owner: Michael Grant 
— provide SDK samples, streaming examples, and assist with tool-calling hooks (Michael to deliver checklist & code snippets by Nov 25).
- Redwood PM/CS owner: Marissa Cole 
— coordinate success criteria, run weekly check-ins, and collect evaluation data (first checkpoint Dec 3).

Immediate next steps:
1) Jordan to confirm owners and accept success criteria (reply by EOD Nov 24).
2) Redwood to send integration checklist + sample SDK (Michael — by Nov 25).
3) Jordan to set up a small staging workload and share access details for telemetry (target Nov 30).

Attachments: acme-integration-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist) 
— will follow with sample code.

Thanks

— integration plan (attachments)

Jordan / Priya 

Great 

 

thanks for confirming. Attaching the integration checklist and sample SDK bundle to help you get started (see attached files). Below is a concise integration plan with implementation steps and recommended API routes/configs.

Integration plan (high level):
1) Auth & environment:
   - Create a POC API key scoped to Acme POC (we'll provision from the Redwood Console).
   - Use staging region: us-west-2.

2) SDK & endpoints:
   - Recommended SDK: redwood-node (we've included sample code).
   - Primary endpoint for streaming chat: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat (bearer auth).
   - For non-streaming batched generation: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

3) Streaming & websocket integration:
   - The streams/chat endpoint returns chunked SSE events; the SDK exposes a readable stream. Example pattern: connect from your backend, pipe tokens to the websocket connection to the browser.
   - If you need CPU-side aggregation, enable incremental KV cache flush every 4 tokens for long conversations.

4) Tool calling (KB lookup flow):
   - We support a tool-calling pattern where model emits a structured call to an external tool. Use the /v1/tools/call endpoint to proxy the call and return results back into the model prompt.
   - Example: when model returns {"tool":"kb_search","query":"..."}, your backend calls Acme KB search, returns results via the SDK callback handler, and Redwood resumes generation.

5) Batching & caching recommendations:
   - Suggest initial batch_size=8 for your traffic profile and enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
   - We'll monitor token distribution in the first 48 hours and propose quantization/batching changes if cost exceeds target.

6) Telemetry & observability:
   - Instrument request IDs (X-Redwood-Request-Id) and forward logs to our Console (we'll share tracing instructions).

Owners & deliverables:
- Michael: attachments + sample SDK and a short streaming example (attached redwood-sdk-sample.zip).
- Marissa: weekly check-in invite (sent) and success criteria tracking sheet (attached checklist).
- Acme: initial smoke test in staging by Nov 30; share telemetry access for Redwood to observe.

Attachments included: acme-integration-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sdk-sample.zip

Let us know if you want an on-call window from Michael during your smoke test 
— he can be available Nov 30 10:00-12:00 PT.

Thanks 

Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: integration plan & streaming example (code + notes)

Jordan 

Following up with the technical bits you asked for. Quick notes + a minimal code snippet below 

Key implementation notes:
- Auth: Bearer token sent in Authorization header. Rotate keys via Console for the POC key.
- Streaming: we expose chunked SSE; the Node SDK emits "token" events. Use a small buffer on the backend to forward tokens to your websocket to avoid head-of-line latency.
- Tool calling: model returns a JSON call object. Your handler should validate tool name and parameters, call your KB (/search endpoint), then call sdk.toolResult(requestId, result) to resume generation.

Minimal Node streaming snippet (pseudo):

const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-node');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });

const stream = await client.streamChat({ model: 'redwood-llama-13b', input: conversation });
stream.on('token', (t) => {
  // forward token to websocket connection
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'token', text: t }));
});
stream.on('end', () => { ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'done' })); });

Tool-calling handler (pseudo):
// inside SDK callback
if (event.type === 'tool_call' && event.tool === 'kb_search') {
  const results = await acmeKb.search(event.args.query);
  await client.sendToolResult(event.requestId, { results });
}

Troubleshooting tips:
- If you see elevated latency, check TLS handshake time and reduce initial model context size.
- If streaming stalls, ensure your websocket consumer processes small payloads and your backend does not batch tokens for >100ms.

I'll be available during the Nov 30 smoke window (10:00-12:00 PT) if you want pair debugging. Reach me at michael.grant@redwood.ai or Slack.

-Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
